about: Which geometry proofs each CI job runs. .claude/skills/generate-gear/proof_shards.py is the only reader: it checks this against `go list` and `go test -list`, emits the workflow matrix, and emits each job's proof/run.sh arguments. Every package and every top-level test belongs to exactly one group, and a name that is added, renamed or removed without an edit here fails the Proof inventory job.
seconds_measured: Seconds the group spent in its "Run the <group> proofs" step on a four-core ubuntu-latest runner with a warm build cache and every test actually executing, from GitHub Actions run 34000135972. About four of those seconds are proof/run.sh building its go.work. Nothing checks these numbers; they record why the split is where it is, and they are what to re-measure before moving a test between groups. The runner varies enough that a difference under about ten seconds is noise.

groups.name: bevelgear-body
groups.why: The bevel sketches, the cone and lattice proofs and the revolved-body solids. TestGearProfiles alone is about half of it.

groups.name: cycloidal
groups.why: The whole cycloidal package, disc and housing together.

groups.name: spurgear
groups.why: The whole spur package, plus every package small enough that its runtime does not matter: the two harnesses, the renderer, the example command and involute, which has no tests and is here so a job still compiles it.

groups.name: twisted-teeth
groups.why: Every gear whose teeth are swept along a twist: the five spiral-bevel slab solids, all of helicalgear and all of herringbonegear. Three packages, so go test overlaps them and the group costs about what its longest one does.
